The code is EWLM. I found it by reading the weights only, without running code, and I haven't confirmed it any other way.

**Where it is.** The last four hidden units (32–35) don't affect play at all. In W2, the columns for those units are all ±0.0 in every one of the 9 output rows. So whatever they compute never reaches the move scores, which makes them a safe place to hide data.

**What's hidden there.** Their biases in b1 are 0.69, 0.87, 0.76 and 0.77. These stand out because the other biases are small, and nothing that trained them could have set them, since the units never touch the output. Reading each value times 100 as an ASCII code gives the letters:

| Unit | b1 | ×100 | ASCII |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 0.69 | 69 | E |
| 33 | 0.87 | 87 | W |
| 34 | 0.76 | 76 | L |
| 35 | 0.77 | 77 | M |

Their rows in W1 are small, regular-looking values (all under 0.5) that look like filler. I tried one other reading: taking the position of each row's largest value as a letter gives C, G, W, M. That isn't a word either, so I went with the cleaner ASCII reading of the biases. One caveat: those biases could be a decoy, with the real code hidden in how the network plays. I couldn't test that without running the network.

CODE: EWLM
